logline: In an alternate history where the Soviet Union landed on the Moon first, the space race never ended - and the consequences ripple through decades of American politics, technology, and human cost.

bollymeter.basis: 75% on RT from 56 critics; a promising alternate-history premise that critics found too cautious in execution - the astronaut ensemble strong, the 1960s NASA texture lovingly rendered, but the potential not yet fully realised.

pull_quotes.text: Though it shoots for the moon and falls somewhere in orbit, the series' impressive alternate history has potential for real liftoff.

seasons.review_body: For All Mankind launched alongside Apple TV+ in November 2019, created by Ronald D. Moore (Battlestar Galactica), Matt Wolpert, and Ben Nedivi. The premise, a Soviet Moon landing forcing NASA to accelerate a space programme that never stopped, stands out for its speculative scope and period detail. The critique centers on execution: the large ensemble and the relationships that take time to earn investment, along with a pace that can feel cautious compared with the show’s ambitions. The 87% audience Popcornmeter outran the review score, suggesting the series connected more readily with viewers through its optimistic alternate-history spirit.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on RT from 27 critics; a season set in the 1980s that fulfilled Season 1's promise completely - Cold War lunar tensions, a richer ensemble, and the show's unique capacity to make alternate history feel personal.

pull_quotes.text: For All Mankind's sophomore flight has compelling character work and a renewed sense of wonder that makes for thrilling viewing.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 jumped to the 1983 Reagan era and reached 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 27 critics. The time-jump format - each season advances the alternate timeline by roughly a decade - gave the show structural elegance and allowed deeper character consequences. The Cold War stakes on the Moon escalated to a genuine political thriller in the final episodes. IndieWire called it the show's full arrival. The audience Popcornmeter stood at 84%. Critics who had qualified Season 1 as promising removed the qualifications - For All Mankind had become one of Apple TV+'s best originals.
seasons.season_over_season: The time-jump to the 1980s sharpens both the political stakes and the character arcs; the show operating confidently at the intersection of speculative history and human drama.

episode_reviews.title: The Grey
episode_reviews.review_body: For All Mankind Season 2 Episode 10 'The Grey' aired April 23, 2021 on Apple TV+ and delivered the Cold War lunar crisis finale that the season had been building toward at maximum pressure. The episode earned the season's place in the 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes consensus from 27 critics by resolving the season's accumulation of alternate-historical tension with emotional consequence rather than spectacle - costs are real, characters are changed, and the status quo shifts rather than resets. IndieWire had described Season 2 as 'the show's full arrival,' and the finale's formal ambition validated that assessment: the lunar confrontation sequence was identified across reviews as the moment For All Mankind demonstrated it belonged among Apple TV+'s best originals rather than just its most ambitious ones. The episode's final scenes, setting up the Season 3 time-jump to the 1990s, positioned the series as one of the few streaming properties whose alternate-history format was actively generating better storytelling rather than just better design.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 2 finale resolved the Cold War lunar crisis in a sequence that lands as one of the most formally ambitious finales Apple TV+ has produced. It is emotionally costly and formally inventive, while also setting up a Season 3 that moves the timeline to an entirely new frontier.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The lunar confrontation sequence - where alternate history and the show's character work converge at maximum pressure.

bollymeter.basis: 94% on RT from 36 critics; the season that pushed the timeline to Mars and added private space industry as a third geopolitical actor - still ambitious, occasionally over-plotted, but unmistakably distinctive television.

pull_quotes.text: For All Mankind's third season goes as far as Mars while maintaining a homey focus on its original ensemble.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 aired June to August 2022, advancing the timeline to 1992 to 1995 and introducing a three-way race to Mars between the US, the Soviets, and a private space company. The addition of private industry complicates the show's ideological framework in ways that land as genuinely thought-provoking, while the season's larger cast spreads emotional focus more thinly than Season 2's tight Cold War thriller. The Popcornmeter sits at 74%, reflecting a slightly less focused feeling than the Season 2 peak.
seasons.season_over_season: Another decade-jump, another successful expansion - Mars race as narrative and private space as new ideological complication; the ensemble stretched but the show's core vision intact.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on RT from 28 critics; the second perfect-score season, set on a permanent Mars colony with a labour revolt as its central drama - critics called it the show's most intellectually ambitious season.

pull_quotes.text: Houston, there's no problem here - For All Mankind's fourth season hones in on what it does best and forges ahead with thought-provoking revisionist history.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 aired November 2023-January 2024 and achieved a second perfect 100% from 28 critics. Set in the early 2000s of the show's alternate timeline, the season planted a functioning Mars colony and organised a workers' uprising as its central political drama - the show's most overtly ideological premise yet, handled with the formal care that had come to define the series. The 83% audience Popcornmeter reflected sustained viewer engagement. Critics who track the show consistently noted that a perfect Tomatometer in back-to-back seasons for a single series is an exceptional critical achievement.
seasons.season_over_season: The second consecutive perfect critical score; the Mars colony as sustained dramatic environment gives the show a new visual grammar and its most explicit class-politics framing.
